connections.why: Algorithms operate on and traverse data structures
Boolean logic underlies the operations a compiler translates
Different paradigms express the same algorithm in different ways
Analysis of requirements feeds directly into system design
A validated design is built into a working, compiled program
IDE tools and translators turn source code into a running program
The language paradigm affects how programs are compiled or interpreted
How data is represented underpins how it is organised and stored
Structured data organisation is the basis of database design
Communication hardware enables data transmission across networks
The operating system enforces data security and access control
Data in transmission must be protected against interception
Hash tables and trees underpin efficient database indexing
Designing data-driven systems requires modelling the database
Legal duties such as data protection drive security requirements
Real-world projects must weigh legal, ethical and economic factors
